nodes.hovertext: Sudden waves of heat, flushing, or sweating may occur during the day or night. Hot flashes affect up to 70% of women, vary by race/ethnicity ~ Rates are high among African-American & Native American women ; Chinese & Japanese women have lower rates & a shorter overall duratiion of hot flashes. Elevated FSH and fluctuating estrogen are predictive of hot flashes.

Sudden waves of heat, flushing, or sweating may occur during the day or night. Hot flashes affect up to 70% of women, vary by race/ethnicity ~ Rates are high among African-American & Native American women ; Chinese & Japanese women have lower rates & a shorter overall duratiion of hot flashes. Elevated FSH and fluctuating estrogen are predictive of hot flashes.
Fluctuation in Estrogen levels could lead to heart palpitations or irregular heart beat.
Dizziness or vertigo may occur, causing a spinning sensation or feeling unsteady. Hormonal fluctuations can affect balance, blood flow, and the inner ear.
Brain fog may cause forgetfulness, slower thinking, or difficulty concentrating. Reduced Estrogen levels and Hormonal fluctuations can affect memory, attention, and mental clarity.
Decline in Progesterone could lead to Memory Lapse.
Decreased attention often due to fluctuating testosterone & estrogen
Migraine/ Headache often caused due to low or absent Progesterone. It is one of the early indicators of Perimenopause.
Fluctuation in testosterone and estrogen can lead to Mood Swings
Fluctuation in estrogen levels can lead to Anxiety
Depressive symptoms varied by ethnicity in SWAN study, with sharp increases over time among Japanese and Hispanic women, and associations with higher testosterone levels
Stress may feel stronger, harder to recover from, and can amplify other symptoms.
Changes in estrogen during perimenopause can disrupt dopamine regulation, which may worsen ADHD symptoms such as inattention, overwhelm, and emotional reactivity.
Panic attacks may become more frequent or intense due to hormonal changes.
Small frustrations can trigger sudden irritability or outbursts due to hormonal fluctuations.

Sleep disruption affects ~38% of women and often co-occurs with hot flashes. Rates vary by race/ethnicity ~ lowest (28%) observed in Japanese and highest (40%) in Caucasian women. Symptoms are also associated with estrogen volatility and low progesterone.
Fatigue may feel persistent or overwhelming, even with adequate rest. Hormonal changes can disrupt sleep, energy regulation, and recovery.
Dreams may become more vivid, intense, or memorable. Hormonal changes can affect sleep cycles and REM sleep, making dreams feel more lifelike.

Libido may increase or decrease during perimenopause. Hormonal fluctuations can affect desire, arousal, energy levels, and comfort. Fluctuations in testosterone and progesterone can lead to decreased Libido
Declining estrogen can weaken pelvic tissues and increase bladder sensitivity, leading to frequent urination.

Vaginal symptoms are common during perimenopause and are associated with declining estrogen levels. 60% of Central American women reported vaginal dryness compared with 21% of non-Hispanic Caucasian women
Decreased Estrogen levels often lead to pain or discomfort during intercourse
Urinary tract infections may occur more often during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect the urinary tract lining and natural protective bacteria.
Hair may become thinner or shed more than usual. Hormonal changes can affect hair growth cycles, leading to noticeable thinning over time.
Acne may appear or worsen during perimenopause. Hormonal shifts can increase oil production and inflammation, leading to breakouts even if acne wasn’t an issue before.
Allergies may appear or worsen during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect immune responses, making the body more sensitive to triggers.
Skin may become drier, itchier, or more sensitive. Hormonal changes can affect collagen, oil production, and skin barrier function.
Nails may become brittle, thin, or prone to breaking as hormonal changes affect keratin production and moisture.
Ears may feel dry or itchy as hormonal changes affect skin moisture and sensitivity.
Bone density may begin to decline as estrogen and testosterone levels fluctuate, increasing the risk of bone loss over time.

Weight gain may occur more easily, especially around the abdomen, even without changes in diet or activity. Hormonal shifts can affect metabolism, fat storage, and insulin sensitivity. Unexplained weight gain is one of the early indicators of Perimenopause.
Body odor may change or become stronger. Hormonal shifts can increase sweating and alter skin bacteria, leading to noticeable changes in scent.
Breast Tenderness are often caused by fluctuations in Progesterone levels. It is one of the early indicators of this stage.
Body aches like Muscle & joint pain
Shoulder stiffness and pain may increase due to hormonal changes.

Tinnitus or Ringing Ear are one of the least discussed symptoms. It may appear or worsen during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect the inner ear and nervous system, leading to ringing or buzzing sounds.
Sudden electric shock-like sensations or internal tremors may occur. These can feel brief but intense and are linked to nervous system sensitivity during hormonal fluctuations.
Insulin resistance may increase during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect how the body processes sugar, making blood glucose harder to regulate.
Dry mouth may occur as hormonal changes affect saliva production, leading to discomfort or a persistent dry sensation.
Menstrual cycles become irregular-shorter, longer, or skipped, as hormone levels fluctuate during this phase.
